name: RFVT2-related Riboflavin Transporter Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for RFVT2 Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of progressive pontobulbar palsy with sensorineural hearing loss
Low plasma riboflavin or flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) levels
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the SLC52A2 gene
Clinical improvement or stabilization upon high-dose riboflavin supplementation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features plus genetic confirmation or biochemical evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical due to potential for treatment response

searchTerms: declining muscle control in face and throat

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cranial nerve neuropathies (especially facial and bulbar nerves)
searchTerms: problems with facial and swallowing nerves

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness predominantly affecting limb girdle muscles
searchTerms: weakness in shoulder and hip muscles

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to diaphragmatic weakness

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy with distal sensory loss
searchTerms: nerve damage causing numbness in hands and feet
nerve damage affecting sensation and movement

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: heart rhythm issues due to autonomic dysfunction
cardiac arrhythmias related to nerve involvement

laboratory: Low plasma riboflavin and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) levels
imaging: MRI brain showing brainstem and cerebellar atrophy
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating sensorimotor neuropathy
other: Clinical improvement with high-dose riboflavin therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Caused by SLC52A3 mutations instead of SLC52A2
Multisystem involvement with mitochondrial DNA mutations
Lack of response to riboflavin supplementation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive bulbar palsy in infancy or childhood
Sensorineural hearing loss combined with cranial neuropathies
Failure to respond to standard neuromuscular treatments
references: Foley AR, et al. Riboflavin transporter deficiency: clinical features and molecular genetics. Brain. 2014.
Green P, et al. Clinical and genetic spectrum of riboflavin transporter deficiency. Neurology. 2016.
Orphanet: RFVT2-related riboflavin transporter deficiency. ORPHA:572543.
